bull_bear.body:
- Mine-to-mouth integrated coal and power model at Maamba provides fuel security, cost stability and independence from global coal market dynamics, while contributing external revenue beyond the captive requirement
- Contracting discipline in Metals: approximately 40% of production sold under long-term annual contracts with Japanese mills and 40-50% under quarterly fixed-base contracts with major Indian steel producers, limiting spot-market exposure to only 10-15% of output
- Long-dated offtake visibility in Zambia - a 20-year PPA with ZESCO supplying power since 2016, plus a signed 20-year PPA for the 100 MW solar project and a PPA covering 100% of Phase II net capacity
- Captive power integration in India, with 144 MW earmarked for captive consumption in ferro alloy production, and downward-revised captive tariffs improving alloy cost competitiveness

- Product-mix flexibility across Silico Manganese and Ferro Silicon, allowing the Metals division to shift furnaces towards whichever alloy market conditions favour
- Deliberate long-cycle capital allocation - deploying capital where barriers to entry are high and staying through the gestation period, producing diversification across geographies, cycles and sectors
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Sector-specific and market risk - ferro alloys exposure to the steel demand cycle, export-market weakness, commodity price volatility, power tariff movements and geopolitical uncertainty — The Metals division's realisations track the steel cycle and export access; during the year EU quota measures, US tariffs and Middle East disruption redirected export-grade material into the domestic market and compressed realisations. Mitigated by continuous monitoring, a flexible product mix, long-term contracts and geographic diversification.
- Commercial risk - pressure on realisations, freight costs, customer payment delays and spot-market exposure — Domestic ferro alloy prices remained subdued with intense competition from marginal players, and payment behaviour of large offtakers directly affects working capital. Mitigated by credit assessment, contractual enforcement, Letter of Credit mechanisms and prudent bidding, with spot exposure held to only 10-15% of output.
- Financial risk - cost and availability of capital, foreign exchange volatility, and deferred tax movements arising from currency appreciation — The Group funds large Zambian projects with tied-up term debt and reports in INR across USD and Kwacha exposures; the Kwacha's appreciation drove a deferred tax provision that materially reduced reported consolidated profit even though it is a timing difference. Mitigated by disciplined capital allocation, project finance discipline, hedging and calibrated dividend decisions.
- Business risk - fuel availability and pricing, manganese ore and reductant availability, and project execution risk — Alloy and power economics both hinge on coal and ore input security, and a large share of group value now sits in projects still under construction. Mitigated by the mine-to-mouth coal model at Maamba, backward integration via the Ivory Coast manganese ore mine and phased project execution.
- Regulatory risk - power sector regulations, Zambian statutory instruments and the Zambia elections in August 2026 — A large part of earnings sits in a single foreign jurisdiction where tariff, tax and statutory frameworks can change, as shown by MEL's power division moving to a 15% effective tax rate on completion of its tax holiday. Mitigated by regulatory engagement, legal and compliance oversight and ring-fencing of USD power assets.
- Counterparty risk - ZESCO payment terms and potential PPA renegotiation — MEL sells power to a single state utility offtaker under a 20-year PPA; arrears had built to US$ 160.6 million before being recovered under an Arbitral Award, with receivables now reduced to US$ 28.0 million. Mitigated by bilateral engagement and the arbitration precedent.
- Environment and climate risk - agriculture exposure to weather and energy transition policies — The new commercial agriculture platform is weather-dependent while the thermal power base faces transition policy pressure, and lower daytime merchant tariffs from rising solar generation plus a projected below-average monsoon are already flagged watch items. Mitigated by insurance, agronomic controls, irrigation, site-level monitoring and diversification into solar.
- Project execution and commissioning concentration - a large pipeline of Zambian projects due within a narrow window — The 100 MW solar plant, the 300 MW Phase II thermal plant, the avocado plantation build-out and the Kawambwa integrated sugar complex are all in construction simultaneously, funded partly by drawn term loans; the Enterprise Risk Management framework identifies project execution risk explicitly and responds with phased project execution.

business.body: Nava manufactures manganese ferro alloys (Silico Manganese and Ferro Silicon) at smelters in Paloncha, Telangana and Dhenkanal, Odisha, and generates thermal power through captive and independent power plants in India and through Maamba Energy Limited in Zambia, which operates the country's only large-scale integrated coal-fired 300 MW power plant alongside its largest coal mine. Alloy output is sold to Japanese steel mills under long-term annual contracts and to major Indian steel producers under quarterly fixed-base contracts, while Zambian power is sold to state utility ZESCO Limited under a 20-year PPA and coal is sold externally to industrial consumers. The Group is also building a commercial agriculture platform in Zambia (avocado plantation and an integrated sugar complex), runs an O&M services business for thermal assets, distributes women's health and wellness products in Southeast Asia, and holds manganese and lithium exploration interests in Cote d'Ivoire and Zambia.

outlook.body:
- Build a diversified, multi-geography enterprise deliberately - each business and geography chosen to build platforms that can endure cycles, generate cash flows and create long-term value, not diversification for its own sake
- Deploy capital where barriers to entry are high, stay through the gestation period, and build assets that generate returns over decades rather than quarters
- Move from building capacity to realising value - repatriating cash from the overseas platform to the Indian balance sheet while the next phase of projects is executed
- Prioritise early commissioning of the committed project pipeline: 400 MW of power capacity addition in Zambia and the avocado plantation
- Extend the power platform into renewables, with a 100 MW solar project marking the Group's entry into a renewable energy portfolio
- Shift the Metals product mix towards Silico Manganese where market conditions are more favourable, using the flexibility of the installed furnace set-up
- Reduce spot-market exposure in Metals through long-term annual contracts with Japanese mills and quarterly fixed-base arrangements with major Indian steel producers
- Structurally shift Indian power towards long-term bilateral contracts and IPP mode - converting 60 MW at Odisha from CPP to IPP and signing a five-year PPA for 50 MW
- Build businesses that reinforce one another - a mine supplying a power plant, that power platform expanding into solar, a metals business securing its own raw material through African exploration, and an agriculture platform whose first harvest already reaches export markets
- Pursue backward integration of manganese ore through African exploration, advancing the Cote d'Ivoire concession towards an exploitation permit
- Consolidate technical support services contracts of Indian group companies at Nava Limited and grow the O&M services mandate across group assets
- Maintain disciplined capital allocation and project-finance discipline, measuring growth by quality of earnings, resilience of cash flows and return on capital rather than size alone
- Nava frames capital allocation as a deliberate, long-cycle discipline: deploy capital where barriers to entry are high, stay through the gestation period and build assets that generate returns over decades rather than quarters. Returns to shareholders are made through dividends - the Board recommended a final dividend of 550%, i.e. `5.50 per equity share of `1 each, for the year ended March 31, 2026, for approval at the 54th AGM, on top of an interim dividend already paid, and unclaimed dividends and the related shares are transferred to the Investor Education and Protection Fund as required. Internally, the Board has adopted policies covering related party transactions, whistle blowing and the determination of material subsidiaries, and maintains an internal control system commensurate with the size, scale and complexity of operations with records maintained in SAP and internal audit observations reported periodically to the Audit Committee. The routed section headed 'Dividend Distribution Policy' contains material-orders, insurance, internal-financial-controls and IEPF disclosures rather than the policy text itself, so no formal payout-ratio or reinvestment policy is stated in the supplied text.
- Diversification into solar power as the stated response to energy transition policy risk - a 100 MW solar project in Zambia under a signed 20-year PPA marks the Group's entry into a renewable energy portfolio
- Energy efficiency initiatives at Maamba Energy Limited reduced auxiliary power consumption to 9.8% from 10.3% in the prior year
- Division A of the avocado plantation received Global Good Agricultural Practices (GAP) certification
- Climate and agronomic controls for the agriculture platform - insurance, agronomic controls, irrigation and site-level monitoring under the Enterprise Risk Management framework
- Enterprise Risk Management framework maintained to identify, evaluate and respond to operational, strategic, financial and regulatory risks, including a Community risk category covering community expectations
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Nava's expansion pipeline is concentrated in Zambia and spans power, renewables and commercial agriculture. Maamba Energy Limited's Phase II 300 MW brownfield thermal power plant is under construction with a capex outlay of USD 400 million, of which US$ 290 million of debt funding is tied up with Zambian banks and financial institutions; commissioning is targeted for Q4 FY 2027 (the January-March 2027 window), the PPA with ZESCO covers 100% of Phase II net capacity at 9.5 US cents per kilowatt hour, Nava Energy Pte Ltd has been appointed O&M Contractor, and at full year operation the plant is expected to generate USD 180-200 million in annual revenues. The 100 MW solar project under Maamba Solar Energy Limited marks the Group's entry into a renewable energy portfolio, with total capex of US$ 90 million and US$ 63 million of debt tied up, commissioning scheduled to commence in July 2026 (targeted July-August 2026), a signed 20-year PPA with ZESCO at 7.80 US cents per kilowatt hour, Nava Energy Zambia Limited as O&M Contractor, and expected revenue of USD 20-22 million at full operation. Together these represent the 400 MW of power capacity addition on which management says early-commissioning focus remains, and the increase in consolidated debt during the year reflects term-loan drawdowns for both projects. In commercial agriculture, the Nava Avocado plantation achieved its first commercial harvest of over 150 MT from Division A exported to South Africa, with over 250,000 plants planted as at March 2026, the full plantation of 400,000 trees to be completed by May 2027, a state-of-the-art packhouse under construction, Global GAP certification for Division A, expected yield of approximately 1,200+ MT in FY 2026-27 roughly doubling each year thereafter through 2034, and a target fruit yield of about 25,000 MT at peak tree maturity. Kawambwa Sugar Limited's integrated sugar complex - sugarcane plantation over 4,500 Ha, 2,500 TCD sugar processing, a 30 KLPD distillery and a 20 MW co-generation power plant - began construction during the year with land development and plantation activity underway and all major packages ordered, targeted for commissioning by March 2028, with debt financing being worked upon with bilateral financial institutions and banks. Overall project progress on the Phase II thermal expansion and avocado plantation crossed the 50% mark during the year and is nearing completion phase by March 2027. Alongside greenfield build-out, the existing base was reconfigured rather than expanded: 60 MW at Odisha was converted from captive to independent power plant mode with effect from 01 November 2025, taking the 150 MW station to 30 MW CPP / 120 MW IPP, and two Telangana furnaces were shifted from Ferro Silicon to Silico Manganese, with the installed metals set-up offering flexibility to produce up to approximately 160,000 MT. Upstream, the Company holds a 340 square kilometre manganese ore concession in Cote d'Ivoire where metallurgical studies are underway ahead of an exploitation permit, and lithium exploration continues in the Mapatizya area of Zambia subject to regulatory clarity on an overlapping licence claim.

- India expected to remain the fastest-growing large steel-demand market in 2026 and 2027, providing a positive backdrop for domestic ferroalloy demand
- Government capital expenditure growth, continuing infrastructure upgrade, strong automobile momentum with GST rationalisation and India's trade deals with developed economies supporting steel-industry momentum
- Domestic ferro alloy market expected to be quite stable given the uptick in Indian steel demand, though continued weak export markets and trade barriers keep pressure on domestic realisations
- Reduction in captive power tariffs expected to improve the competitiveness and margins of the Metals division

- Management does not anticipate any reason for ferro alloy prices to fall meaningfully below the preceding year on a full-year basis, though pricing remains fluid
- Indian power demand growth driven by robust economic expansion, urbanisation and increased local manufacturing, with emerging demand from electric vehicles, data centres and AI-driven infrastructure
- Availability of medium-term PPA, lower Singareni coal prices and the conversion of 60 MW into IPP to compound through FY 2026-27
- Watch item: reduced merchant tariffs during daytime on power exchanges due to a substantial increase in solar generation, plus a projected below-average monsoon and dry spells, affecting remunerative tariffs
- Power deficit in Zambia and Southern African nations keeps MEL's 300 MW plant operating at full capacity; commissioning of the 100 MW solar and 300 MW thermal plants may reduce those deficits and boost economic activity
- Group to see additional revenues during the year from the expected commissioning of the 100 MW solar and 300 MW thermal plants, while lower ECL reversal and Kwacha appreciation will weigh on MEL's power division profitability
- Demand for high grade coal expected to increase with improved economic activity as power deficits reduce; competition from nearby mines addressed through increased marketing efforts and pricing strategy
- Avocado yields scaling with tree growth, with Division B expected to give a trial yield in the current year
- Ferro alloys industry closely linked to the steel demand cycle, with divergence across regions - China declining while developing economies, ASEAN, MENA and Africa show renewed momentum
- Approximately 40% of Metals production sold under long-term annual contracts with Japanese mills and 40-50% under quarterly fixed-base contracts with major Indian steel producers, limiting spot-market exposure to only 10-15% of output
- Maamba Energy Limited holds a 20-year Power Purchase Agreement with ZESCO Limited, supplying power since 2016
- PPA with ZESCO for 100% of Phase II net capacity is in place at 9.5 US cents per kilowatt hour
- 20-year PPA with ZESCO for the 100 MW solar project signed at 7.80 US cents per kilowatt hour
- Five-year Power Purchase Agreement for 50 MW of Odisha capacity starting February 2026, plus bilateral contracts supporting Indian merchant power volumes
- Nava Energy Pte Ltd appointed O&M Contractor for MEL's Phase II 300 MW expansion and Nava Energy Zambia Limited appointed O&M Contractor for MSEL's 100 MW solar project
- All major packages for the Kawambwa integrated sugar complex have been ordered

Commission the avocado packhouse to strengthen the ability to manage quality, storage and market timing.
Avocado plantation is expected to yield approximately 1,200+ MT in FY 2026-27, with volumes expected to approximately double each year thereafter through 2034.
The 300 MW Phase II expansion at Maamba is targeted for commissioning in Q4 FY27.

Avocado fruit yield from Division A is expected to scale to 1,200+ MT in FY 2026-27 from approximately over 150 MT in FY 2025-26, with progressive scaling thereafter and Division B expected to give a trial yield in the current year.
Reduced daytime merchant tariffs on power exchanges from higher solar generation, together with a projected below-average monsoon and dry spells, have to be watched for remunerative tariffs.
Lower ECL reversal and appreciation of the Zambian Kwacha will impact the profitability of MEL's power division in the current year.
Management does not anticipate any reason for ferro alloy prices to fall meaningfully below the preceding year on a full-year basis.
Captive power tariffs have been revised downwards on lower Singareni coal prices and better Odisha plant parameters, with the positive effect to be seen in FY 2026-27.

Commission MEL's Phase II 300 MW brownfield thermal power plant in Zambia, with a capex outlay of USD 400 million of which US$ 290 million of debt is tied up with Zambian banks and financial institutions.
Phase II 300 MW plant carries a capex outlay of USD 400 million with US$ 290 million of debt funding already tied up with Zambian banks and financial institutions.
The Phase II 300 MW thermal expansion and the avocado plantation projects crossed the 50% overall progress mark during the year and are to near completion phase by March 2027.

wtt.tone_latest: Confident on the strong quarter, buyback and project revenue visibility; candid about domestic power price weakness and ferro alloys being low-margin, deflected on steady-state EBITDA/ROCE and exact discovery timelines.

meta.thesis: Cash-rich, founder-run conglomerate where Zambian thermal IPP (Maamba) drives consolidated profit and funds a multi-pronged diversification (300MW thermal expansion, 100MW solar, sugar, avocado, lithium/mineral exploration), while the domestic Indian power and ferro-alloy businesses face a softening price cycle.
